intro_en: The Israel National Trail advances along the southern bank and above the channel of Nahal Tze'elim, one of the large streams that cross the Judean Desert. Alongside the impressive scenery of the Nahal Tze'elim canyon, in the middle of the segment the Dead Sea and Mount Masada are revealed before us.
character_en: Mostly comfortable, moderate walking, with few ascents or descents
important_en: Hiking is forbidden on days with a flash-flood risk!
For those wishing to include a visit to Masada, there is an entrance fee. The national park closes at 16:00 during winter time.
description_en:
The Israel National Trail starts from the southern side of the Brekhat Tzfira overnight campsite, together with a red-marked trail. Before turning onto the red trail, it is recommended to take a short out-and-back walk along a blue-marked trail that leaves from the other side of the campsite to a fine lookout over Brekhat Tzfira (Tzfira Pool), the rock pools and the waterfall (it is not possible to descend to the pool from this lookout).
The trail begins its course along the southern bank of Nahal Tze'elim with an easy climb. During the first half of the day we hike along a terrace above the southern wall of the canyon. The track crosses small tributaries of the Tze'elim. Geologically, the trail passes through the gentle landscape formed by the soft rock formations (Mount Scopus Group), beneath which lie the harder and older rock formations (Judea Group) into which the canyon is cut.
As the trail approaches the rim of the canyon, views open up over the winding channel and the impressive canyon walls. Across the canyon you can look out over the expanses of the desert plateau. In the distance are three cone-shaped mountains, Itai, Ribai and Hidai, named after King David's heroes. Rising high right above the canyon is Har Namer.
Along the way we meet a blue trail descending from Givat Gorni, and further on a green trail that descends to Brekhat Na'ama, a large rock pool in the stream channel, also crosses the trail.
The Israel National Trail continues with the red trail to the top of Ma'ale Inbal. Here the red trail descends to Ma'ale Inbal, while the Israel National Trail continues to the right through gentle terrain until it meets a blue trail. The blue trail arrives from the left, from Ma'ale Inbal, and it will accompany the Israel National Trail as far as the track to the Masada entrance road.
From here the trail begins to curve right towards the south, and after a short distance makes a short descent into the channel of Nahal Inbal. Before the descent it is worth going to the lookout from a high rock platform to the right of the trail.
From the lookout point, to the north, the fault escarpment is visible as far as the Ein Gedi area. Deep below us is the channel of Nahal Tze'elim, emerging from the canyon into the Dead Sea rift. To the east we can see young date plantations planted in the area of the Nahal Tze'elim estuary, and to their right the water pumping station that pumps Dead Sea water from the northern basin into the canal through which the water flows south to the Dead Sea Works evaporation ponds. To the south and east is "the Lisan" (the tongue), a pale raised area above the waterline. The light-blue water at the foot of the Lisan and southward is the evaporation ponds of the Israeli and Jordanian Dead Sea works.
Far to the east, beyond the sea and the Lisan, is the ridge of the Moab Mountains in Jordanian territory. The flat-topped mountain to the south is Masada. On the left side of the mountain you can make out the rock terraces of the "Northern Palace", and on the mountain's western face "rests" a pale ramp, the siege ramp built by the Romans. South of Masada we see Mount Elazar.
We continue walking and descend with the trail into the channel of Nahal Inbal; the stream is cut into hard limestone and so is somewhat canyon-like. The walls on the sides of the channel make it possible to find a shady corner for a break and a rest.
From here, the trail leads through gentle terrain to the western entrance road to Masada from the direction of Arad. A little before the blue trail joins the road, the Israel National Trail turns left onto a short descent that leads to the western entrance gate of Masada National Park.
Lodging recommendations
Masada West overnight campsite: an overnight spot with showers, for a fee. Requires coordination with the Israel Nature and Parks Authority (telephone 08-6280404, extension 1).
nearby_en: Brekhat Tzfira: an additional walk of about 4 km with challenging sections and metal rungs.
Points of interest: lookout over Brekhat Tzfira. Views over the Nahal Tze'elim canyon and the Judean Desert plateau. View of the Dead Sea and Masada. Crossing Nahal Inbal.
author_en: Itzik Ben Dov, trail marking coordinator, Society for the Protection of Nature in Israel.
